questions.question: Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice. The letter will be delivered by the postman tomorrow.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the following sentence in active voice.

The letter will be delivered by the postman tomorrow.

options.text: The postman delivered the letter tomorrow

options.text: The postman will have delivered the letter tomorrow.

options.text: The postman will deliver the letter tomorrow.
options.html: The postman will deliver the letter tomorrow.

options.text: The postman will be delivering the letter tomorrow.
options.html: The postman will be delivering the letter tomorrow.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Future Indefinite. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Future Indefinite.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + shall/will + be + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + shall/will + V1 + Object.

For example:

The assignment will be completed by him. (Passive Voice)

He will complete the assignment. (Active Voice)

The options except (3) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Active Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is: "The postman will deliver the letter tomorrow."

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. O. delicious R. she Q. a P. baked S. chocolate cake
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

O. delicious

R. she

Q. a

P. baked

S. chocolate cake
questions.solution:
Subject: The sentence starts with R (she) because it is the subject performing the action.

Starting point: She

Verb: Next, we need the action word, which is P (baked).

Progress: She baked

Object Determiner: The article Q (a) comes next to introduce what was baked.

Progress: She baked a

Adjective: The word O (delicious) describes the object and logically follows the article.

Progress: She baked a delicious

Object: Finally, we add the object S (chocolate cake) to complete the sentence.

Complete Sentence: "She baked a delicious chocolate cake."

Thus, the correct sequence is RPQOS.

questions.question: In the given question, a statement divided into different segments is given. Rearrange all the segments to form a coherent statement. Q: the administration of the country

S: after Pakistan framed
questions.solution:

questions.question: Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph. A. It is also called a nuclear family. B. It is good to be in a small family because there is better management of resources. C. A small family is one with parents and a maximum of two children. D. The advantages of a small family are numerous.
questions.questionHtml:
Sentences of a paragraph are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the sentences in the correct order to form a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

A. It is also called a nuclear family.

B. It is good to be in a small family because there is better management of resources.

C. A small family is one with parents and a maximum of two children.

D. The advantages of a small family are numerous.
questions.solution:
C: "A small family is one with parents and a maximum of two children." - This introduces the definition of a small family.

A: "It is also called a nuclear family." - This follows naturally as it provides an alternate term for the concept introduced in the first sentence.

D: "The advantages of a small family are numerous." - This shifts the focus to the benefits of a small family.

B: "It is good to be in a small family because there is better management of resources." - This elaborates on one of the advantages mentioned in the previous sentence.

Thus, the sequence CADB forms a meaningful and coherent paragraph.

questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error. No other place in this country is so better as Gulmarg, Kashmir.
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

No other place in this country is so better as Gulmarg, Kashmir.
questions.solution:
The phrase "so better as" is grammatically incorrect. The correct phrase should be "as good as" because:

"Better" is the comparative form of "good," and it is used with "than" (e.g., "better than").

To compare equality, we use the structure "as...as" with the positive degree of the adjective, i.e., "as good as."

Corrected Sentence: "No other place in this country is as good as Gulmarg, Kashmir."
